sections.h2: Where is Pine Bluff and what is the area like?
sections.html:
Pine Bluff is the seat of Jefferson County in southeast Arkansas, on the Arkansas River in the Delta lowlands. The county sits about 43 miles southeast of Little Rock and borders Lonoke, Arkansas, Lincoln, Cleveland, Grant and Pulaski counties.

The city covers roughly 46 square miles at an elevation of 226 feet, and the terrain is flat farmland and river bottom. Water shapes the map: the Arkansas River, Lake Pine Bluff, Lake Langhofer at the slack water harbor, and Bayou Bartholomew on the western edge, where the Delta gives way to the Timberlands.

The city runs on a mayor-council system with an eight-member council, two members from each of four wards. A seller who needs to deal with the city on a permit or a code notice will be working with that government rather than the county, so it helps to know which office sent a letter.

Pine Bluff began as a river settlement after the flood of 1819 and was officially named by the county court on October 16, 1832. It was incorporated on January 8, 1839, and the first railroad arrived in December 1873.

Cotton and river trade made it the third-largest city in Arkansas by 1890. Jefferson County produced 55,120 bales of cotton in 1886, the most of any county in the state. Victorian-style houses were built west of Main Street as personal fortunes grew from the 1870s.

The Army broke ground on the Pine Bluff Arsenal on December 2, 1941, on about 15,000 acres north of the city. Later, a kraft paper mill was announced in 1957, and the Port of Pine Bluff anchors the Harbor Industrial District along the river.

A city that has been building since the 1830s has houses from many eras. A Victorian-era house west of Main Street and a newer house on the edge of town raise different repair questions, and a cash buyer prices them separately.

sections.h2: What has happened to Pine Bluff's population?
sections.html:
Pine Bluff has lost population for five decades, falling from a peak of about 57,400 in 1970 to an estimated 38,213 in 2025. For a seller, a shrinking city is context worth knowing before setting a price.

Jefferson County shows the same pattern. It peaked at 90,718 in 1980, counted 67,260 in 2020, and has an estimated 62,987 in 2025. The 2020 housing count for the city was 19,197 units, with 16.2% of them vacant and 16,086 households.

With 16.2% of units vacant, some owners find a house hard to sell, and an inherited house can sit while taxes keep coming due.

sections.h2: Who employs people in Pine Bluff?
sections.html:
Pine Bluff's largest employers are a mix of health care, banking, food processing, packaging and government. The list includes:

  • Jefferson Regional Medical Center
  • Simmons First National Corp.
  • Tyson Foods
  • Evergreen Packaging
  • The Pine Bluff Arsenal
  • Union Pacific Railroad
  • The Saracen Casino Resort, completed in 2020 at a cost of $350 million, with more than 1,100 full-time staff

The area's farm output includes cotton, soybeans, cattle, rice, poultry, timber and catfish. The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff is the state's second-oldest public institution, and Southeast Arkansas College offers two-year and technical programs.

If you own a rental house, which employers sit nearest to it is a fair thing to mention to a buyer.

sections.h2: Which Pine Bluff school districts and roads matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Three public districts serve the city: Pine Bluff, Watson Chapel and White Hall. The Dollarway School District merged into Pine Bluff on July 1, 2021, and Dollarway High School closed in 2023. Because a street can sit in any of these districts, a seller should confirm the district of the address before quoting it.

Interstate 530 is the southern bypass, and U.S. 63, 65, 79, 270 and 425 also run through the area, along with Arkansas Highways 15, 54, 81, 190 and 365. Grider Field is a general airport about 4 miles southeast of town, and Clinton National in Little Rock handles most commercial flights. Pine Bluff Transit runs six routes, and Union Pacific provides freight rail.

Dollarway Road, completed in 1914, was the longest continuous stretch of concrete road in the country at that time.

sections.h2: What does Pine Bluff's flood history mean for a house?
sections.html:
Pine Bluff's flat river-delta location means flood history is a fair question for any buyer. The Great Flood of 1927 flooded most of northern and southeastern Jefferson County and broke levees, and the 1933 Mississippi River flood displaced residents who relocated to Pine Bluff.

The Army Corps of Engineers built a levee to keep the river's main channel near the city, and the channel eventually shifted away and left an oxbow that became Lake Pine Bluff. A levee system now runs 380 miles from Pine Bluff to Venice, Louisiana.

The city averages about 53.6 inches of rain a year over roughly 97 days, with a mean daily high of 73.2 degrees and a record high of 112. Humidity, heat and heavy rain make roof condition, drainage and crawl space moisture the main issues in an older house here. Check FEMA's flood map for the specific address before a sale, because the ground you stand on matters more than the city name.

sections.h2: How does Jefferson County handle property tax?
sections.html:
The Jefferson County Tax Collector, at 101 West Barraque in Pine Bluff, collects property and real estate taxes, municipal liens and business personal property tax. Its filing season runs from March 1 to October 15 each year, and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 5:00 pm. The phone number is 870-541-5313.

State rules apply on top of that. The state reappraises property every 3, 4 or 5 years, and the deadline to schedule a hearing with the County Board of Equalization is the third Monday in August. Homestead owners can claim a credit of up to $500 a year, rising to up to $600 with 2026 tax bills, and the taxable value of a homestead cannot rise more than 5% a year under Amendment 79.

Taxes that go unpaid can lead to a sale by the Commissioner of State Lands. In 2023 that office sold just over 200 Jefferson County properties, most for under $500, and as of October 28, 2024, 40 Pine Bluff properties were offered at an online auction after failing to sell at the first one. If you owe back taxes on a house you want to sell, start with the collector before the delinquency grows.

sections.h2: What vacant-property and code issues do Pine Bluff sellers face?
sections.html:
Pine Bluff is one of three Delta cities that worked with Community Progress for about 18 months on strategies for vacant, abandoned and deteriorated properties, and Jefferson County is among the 20 Arkansas counties with the highest residential vacancy rates.

  • The urban renewal agency and the code enforcement department hold "Green Sweeps" to teach owners about maintenance duties.
  • The urban renewal agency and public works host monthly free dump days for large household items.
  • An owner who lives elsewhere should keep up the yard and secure the building, since those are the maintenance duties these events focus on.

Arkansas does not require every seller to complete a disclosure form, according to the Arkansas Real Estate Commission, but listing agents must make reasonable efforts to learn material facts. On a transfer, the state charges $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration through a recorded stamp, and Justia's copy of the statute shows an additional $2.20 per $1,000 assigned to the purchaser.

Selling as-is to a cash buyer removes the need to clean, repair and stage a vacant house, which is why this route is common for inherited and out-of-town ownership here.

faqs.q: How many people live in Pine Bluff?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 38,213 residents as of July 1, 2025. The 2020 census counted 41,253 and the 2010 census counted 49,083.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Jefferson County property tax?
faqs.a: Pay at the Jefferson County Tax Collector, 101 West Barraque in Pine Bluff, or by phone at 870-541-5313. The filing season runs from March 1 to October 15.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Pine Bluff house in?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. The city is served by the Pine Bluff, Watson Chapel and White Hall districts, and Dollarway merged into Pine Bluff on July 1, 2021.

faqs.q: What happens to a Pine Bluff house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: It can be certified for the Commissioner of State Lands and sold at the annual sale. Properties that do not sell move to a post-auction list.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited Pine Bluff house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. An as-is sale to a cash buyer lets you skip repairs and cleanup, and the buyer deals with the condition. Gather the deed and the latest tax statement first.
